original_question: Is there a satisfactory theory of Polish pro-Lie groups, separable pro-Lie groups, or compactly generated pro-Lie groups, especially in the connected case?
target_in_paper: §9, Question 12: "Is there a satisfactory theory of Polish pro-Lie groups (respectively, separable pro-Lie groups, or compactly-generated pro-Lie groups), notably in the connected case?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact open problem. It correctly identifies the three classes named in the paper—Polish pro-Lie groups, separable pro-Lie groups, and compactly generated pro-Lie groups—and it correctly preserves the paper's special emphasis on the connected case.
missing_details: The official formulation is an open-ended request for a "satisfactory theory," not specifically a classification theorem, structure theorem, or existence theorem.

To make the question stand-alone, "pro-Lie group" should be specified in the paper's sense: a topological group isomorphic to a closed subgroup of an arbitrary product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups.
The paper poses three parallel cases separately—Polish pro-Lie groups, separable pro-Lie groups, and compactly generated pro-Lie groups—rather than one merged class.
For full self-containment, it helps to define "Polish" as separable and completely metrizable, and "compactly generated" in the usual topological-group sense of being generated by a compact subset.
The paper's wording is "notably in the connected case"; your "especially in the connected case" is faithful in substance but not verbatim.

A nearby contextual remark is that the Abelian case is discussed in the reference book [5], pp. 235ff.; the paper's open question asks for a broader satisfactory theory beyond that existing Abelian discussion.
There are no ambient field/ring parameters, degree conditions, nilpotency assumptions, or asymptotic quantifiers hidden in this problem; the setting is purely that of topological/pro-Lie groups.
refined_question: For pro-Lie groups in the sense of Hofmann and Morris—that is, topological groups isomorphic to closed subgroups of arbitrary products of finite-dimensional real Lie groups—is there a satisfactory theory of (i) Polish pro-Lie groups (separable completely metrizable pro-Lie groups), (ii) separable pro-Lie groups, and (iii) compactly generated pro-Lie groups (pro-Lie groups generated by a compact subset), notably in the connected case?
justification: The nearest official target is exactly §9, Question 12, and your draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of it. The only real refinements needed are to make the paper's notion of pro-Lie group explicit, preserve the fact that the question is asked in three parallel variants, and add standard definitions so the problem is self-contained. The surrounding context explains why the connected case is singled out: connected pro-Lie groups are treated in the survey as a natural extension of connected locally compact groups. The paper does not give an equivalent reformulation of Question 12; it only adds the nearby remark that the Abelian case is discussed in the reference book [5], pp. 235ff.
